transformations.edit: Extracted the target-local ChunksExact representation with private `v`, `rem`, and `chunk_size` fields, preserving field names, order, types, and privacy while omitting Rust stability/doc attributes.
Included ChunksExact::new with the real Rust body order: `let rem = slice.len() % chunk_size; let fst_len = slice.len() - rem; let (fst, snd) = ...; Self { v: fst, rem: snd, chunk_size }`.

Adapted the helper's `unsafe { slice.split_at_unchecked(fst_len) }` to the reviewed vstd `slice.split_at(fst_len)` contract after proving `fst_len <= slice.len()`; this exposes the same prefix/suffix data flow at the valid index and is recorded as a minimal split boundary.
Adapted the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &[T]` parameter and named return for Verus; the executable target body remains assert then ChunksExact::new(slice, chunk_size).
Converted Rust `assert!(chunk_size != 0, ...)` to Verus `assert(chunk_size != 0)` under the same generated precondition; no control-flow path is removed.

Defined the closed iterator-view helper from the extracted `v`, `rem`, and `chunk_size` fields to expose source as `v + rem`, remaining as `v`, empty yielded prefix, suffix remainder, requested chunk size, and forward direction.
Inlined the generated shared vocabulary predicates `slice_iterator_well_formed` and `slice_chunk_partition` so Verus can check the exact postcondition against the source-backed iterator view.

Added proof-only arithmetic, sequence-split, and reveal annotations to discharge `rem < chunk_size`, divisibility of the first partition, and prefix/suffix recomposition; these have no executable data-flow or evaluation-order effect.
